Trick-or-Treat Bag Proofs

All 13 student designs, one page each. Every page describes the design, what already works, and a checklist of edits to make in Canva before it goes to the heat press. Each design is previewed on the natural, off-white canvas bag so you can see how the tan color changes it.

Sampler Small fixes

Printing on natural canvas

The bags are an earth-tone off-white, not bright white. That changes how every design prints.

Check the bags are sublimation blanks

Sublimation ink only bonds to polyester. Plain 100% cotton canvas won’t hold it and the print washes out. Make sure the bags are sold as sublimation (poly or poly-blend) canvas.

The bag color mixes into every color

Sublimation ink is see-through, so the tan canvas tints the whole design. Blues turn teal, pinks go peachy, lavender goes dusty. Bold, dark colors change the least.

White prints as tan

Sublimation has no white ink. Anything white in a design comes out the color of the bag, so white text needs a dark background or a dark outline to show.

White backgrounds blend in, full backgrounds make a patch

Designs on a white background look printed straight onto the canvas. Designs with a colored background print as a square patch with a hard edge. Both work; just center patches carefully.

Mirror before printing

Flip the design horizontally on the transfer paper, or every word will come out backwards on the bag.

Keep an inch clear

Keep titles and faces at least an inch from the edges. Bags shift a little in the press, and the edges land near seams and handles.

Test the dark designs first

Big areas of black and navy can press uneven on canvas. Run one test bag before a batch of the dark designs (Bag, 5, 6).

Only art you’re allowed to sell

Brand logos, game screenshots and movie characters can’t go on bags for sale. Canva’s own elements are usually fine, but check the element’s license if unsure.

Trick or treat Bag

Full Moon Spiders

Small fixesA few edits in Canva

What’s on it

A navy night sky with a huge glowing yellow moon in the center. Two big black spider silhouettes crawl across the bottom between twisted bare trees, with small carved jack-o’-lanterns in each corner. Cobwebs hang in the top corners and two yellow bats flank the blue "HAPPY HALLOWEEN" title. A small line reads "have a good halloween," and the black strip at the bottom holds a website address.

What works

  • The moon gives the whole design a strong center that reads from across a room.
  • Silhouettes (spiders, trees, pumpkins) print crisply because they are solid black.

Fix before pressing

  • Delete "www.reallygreatsite.com". That is Canva’s placeholder text from the template, and it will print on every bag.
  • The blue title fades into the navy sky at "HA" and "EEN". Change it to orange or white with a thick black outline so every letter shows.
  • Move the two bats so they sit beside the title instead of on top of the H and N.
  • The two cobwebs don’t match (one white, one blue). Make both white.
  • Either make "have a good halloween" bigger and capitalized, or remove it. At this size it will be hard to see on a bag.
  • Use the empty black strip for something useful, like "Trick or Treat!" in orange.
  • The navy background covers the whole square, so it prints as a dark patch with a hard edge on the tan bag. Center it carefully in the press.

Bag 1

Whoppers Table

Can't sell as isUses someone else’s artwork

What’s on it

A photo-style scene of a cozy Halloween table: carved pumpkins, a fireplace, a candle in a "Witches Brew" cauldron, a jar of candy pumpkins, and chocolate bats on a purple spiderweb tablecloth. The center is a box of Whoppers candy decorated with witch hats. Ornate "Trick or Treat (Special Halloween Collection)" lettering floats above.

What works

  • Rich, warm colors and a strong Halloween mood.
  • The purple and orange palette ties together well.

Fix before pressing

  • The Whoppers box is a real brand (owned by Hershey). The logo and packaging can’t go on bags we sell.
  • The small print on the box is AI-scrambled ("EADBORS", "SCNSORS") and looks like a mistake up close.
  • Replace the box with a generic candy bowl or a pile of wrapped candy, and keep the pumpkins, cauldron and tablecloth.
  • "Special Halloween Collection" makes it sound like a product line. Shorten the title to just "Trick or Treat."
  • The whole image is dark and detailed. Sublimation on canvas softens fine detail, so expect it to print a bit muddier than on screen.

Bag 2

Hooded Skull

Needs reworkGood idea, needs building out

What’s on it

A hooded figure in a white cloak with a grinning skull face and glowing blue eyes, set in a misty gray hallway. The picture sits as a square inside a white border. Thin blue text at the top reads "Halloween" and "Trick or Treat," with part of "Trick" in pink.

What works

  • The glowing eyes are a real eye-catcher.
  • The cool blue and gray palette is different from the other bags, which helps it stand out on a table.

Fix before pressing

  • The text is too thin to read on a bag. Switch to a bold font and make it bigger.
  • Only "ick" in "Trick" is pink, which looks like an accident. Pick one color for all the words.
  • The words sit on top of the hood. Move them into the white border above or below the picture so the face stays clear.
  • This is scary for little trick-or-treaters. It could be marketed to teens and adults, or paired with a friendlier design.
  • The white border will print as the bag’s tan color, so the picture sits in a beige frame. Either keep that look on purpose, or stretch the image to fill the square.

Bag 3

Haunted House

Ready to pressSmall polish only

What’s on it

A black haunted mansion with glowing orange windows on a dark red background. Big white brush-stroke letters across the middle say "TRICK-OR-TREAT." Along the bottom are orange tombstones, a black cat with green eyes, a jack-o’-lantern and a cartoon vampire kid. Pumpkins hang from branches in the top corners.

What works

  • The strongest bold design in the set. The title is huge and readable.
  • Orange, black and red are classic Halloween colors and print well.
  • The cat and the vampire kid keep it friendly for young children.

Fix before pressing

  • The two hanging pumpkins on the right are dark blue on dark red and nearly disappear. Make them orange or white like the left side.
  • The left branch is white and the right branch is black. Make them match.
  • The hyphens in the title cut through two windows. Nudge the text up a little.
  • Sublimation can’t print white, so the white letters will come out the tan color of the bag. They still read well against the dark red, and a thin black outline would make them crisper.
  • The red background prints as a square patch with a hard edge on the tan bag. Center it carefully.

Bag 4

Peeking Cats Party

Small fixesA few edits in Canva

What’s on it

A soft pink background with two giant black cats with yellow eyes peeking up from the bottom and left side. Cute googly-eyed spiders dangle on strings everywhere, with two smiling pumpkins in the middle, a witch on a broom, a flock of bats and a small skull with leaves. A row of stars and pumpkins runs across the top, and the title says "HALLOWEEN PARTY."

What works

  • Fun and friendly. The peeking cats are a great idea.
  • Pink is a nice change from the usual orange and black.

Fix before pressing

  • It says "Party" instead of "Trick or Treat." Change the words if this is going on the treat bags.
  • The title is small compared to everything else. Make it about twice as big.
  • A star covers the W, and spider strings cross "EEN". Clear the area behind the title.
  • There are about 14 spiders. Cutting it to 5 or 6 will make the cats and pumpkins stand out.
  • The small cat in the top-left corner is cut off. Remove it or move it fully onto the design.
  • Pale pink mixed with the tan bag turns peachy. Either deepen the pink a few shades, or accept a warm peach look.

Bag 5

Moon Wolf

Small fixesA few edits in Canva

What’s on it

A black wolf with amber eyes standing on a dark hill under a starry blue sky, with a large gray full moon in the upper right. Drawn in a smooth cartoon style. There is no text.

What works

  • Calm, cool and well drawn. Appeals to older kids and adults.
  • The moon and stars give it a clear night-time feel.

Fix before pressing

  • Nothing says Halloween yet. Add a title like "Happy Howl-o-ween" in orange across the black hill.
  • The wolf’s legs and paws blend into the black hill. Lighten the hill to dark blue, or add a thin light edge around the wolf.
  • Add one or two Halloween details, like a small pumpkin at the wolf’s feet or a few bats near the moon.
  • This design is almost all dark ink and fills the square, so it prints as a dark patch on the tan bag. Do a test press to check the black doesn’t come out blotchy.

Bag 6

Moon Village (Background)

Needs reworkGood idea, needs building out

What’s on it

A dark blue night sky with a bright yellow moon cut off in the top-left corner. Very faint silhouettes of churches, houses and bare trees sit along the bottom, and a solid black strip runs across the bottom edge. There is no text or characters.

What works

  • The glowing moon is pretty and matches the moon on the first bag.
  • It makes a good background to build a design on.

Fix before pressing

  • Right now this is a background, not a finished design. It needs a title and a main picture.
  • The village silhouettes are so faint they will vanish when printed. Make them solid black.
  • Add a focus in the open space on the right, such as a witch flying past the moon or a row of jack-o’-lanterns.
  • Put "Trick or Treat" in the black strip at the bottom in orange or yellow.

Bag 7

Pumpkin Witch

Ready to pressSmall polish only

What’s on it

A pink-to-purple gradient background with cobwebs across the top and black spiders hanging down both sides. In the center is a cute little character with a pumpkin head and a big black witch hat, holding a jack-o’-lantern. Big bright aqua letters say "Happy Halloween." Haunted houses, bats and tiny zombie hands sit in the bottom corners.

What works

  • Balanced and neat: the character, title and corners each have their own space.
  • The pumpkin witch is cute and will appeal to young kids.
  • The title is thick and easy to read.

Fix before pressing

  • On the tan bag the aqua letters shift toward green-teal. Orange with a black outline would hold its color better, or keep teal on purpose as the "different" bag.
  • The gradient fills the whole square, so it prints as a purple patch with hard edges on the tan bag, and the pale yellow corner will nearly vanish. Center it carefully when pressing.
  • The top cobweb goes right to the edge. Keep it at least an inch in from the edge so it isn’t lost in the seam.

Bag 8

Witch Hat Pumpkins

Small fixesA few edits in Canva

What’s on it

A big smiling jack-o’-lantern at the top with four yellow pumpkins wearing purple witch hats around it. Orange "HAPPY" sits over the jack-o’-lantern and large white "HALLOWEEN" has a gray drop shadow. "October 2026" is in dark blue, and an orange fence with twisted trees frames the bottom corners.

What works

  • Bright orange, yellow and purple hold up well on the tan bag.
  • The witch-hat pumpkins are a fun, repeating character.

Fix before pressing

  • "HALLOWEEN" is white, and white doesn’t print. On the tan bag the letters disappear and only the gray shadow shows. Give the letters a purple or black fill, or a thick dark outline.
  • "HAPPY" covers the jack-o’-lantern’s mouth. Move the pumpkin up or the word down so they don’t overlap.
  • Replace "October 2026" with "Trick or Treat!" A date makes the bag feel out of date next year.
  • There is a big empty band between the title and the date. Tighten the spacing or make the title bigger.

Bag 9

Graveyard Sketch

Ready to pressSmall polish only

What’s on it

A hand-drawn marker-style scene: a twisted purple tree, purple tombstones (some with crosses), a shovel, bats, and five orange jack-o’-lanterns in the grass. "Happy Halloween" is written above in drippy black letters. Plenty of white space around it.

What works

  • Looks hand-made, which is a great selling point for a student business.
  • The purple and orange match each other and print well on white.
  • The white background disappears into the tan bag, so the drawing looks printed right on the canvas with no square edge.

Fix before pressing

  • The drawing could be a bit bigger to fill the square. Scale it up about 10%.
  • Try the title in purple to tie it to the drawing, or keep it black if you prefer the contrast.
  • Optional: add "Trick or Treat" under the pumpkins in the same drippy style.

Bag 10

Headless Horseman

Can't sell as isUses someone else’s artwork

What’s on it

A glowing, see-through ghost rider on a ghost horse in a dark rocky forest. The rider has no head and holds a sword up high. A white speech bubble says "Where is my head."

What works

  • The joke is funny and gets a laugh.
  • The ghostly glow is a nice spooky effect.

Fix before pressing

  • This looks like a screenshot from a video game. The game company owns that picture, so it can’t be printed and sold.
  • The image is small and blurry. Stretched to bag size it will look pixelated.
  • Keep the joke: rebuild it with a headless horseman silhouette from Canva’s elements on a night background.
  • The words run past the edge of the speech bubble. Make the bubble bigger, use a bolder font, and add a "?" at the end.

Bag 11

Purple Title & Pumpkin

Ready to pressSmall polish only

What’s on it

Chunky lavender "HAPPY HALLOWEEN" letters with a thick dark outline and little orange bats flying around them. A large classic jack-o’-lantern with a green stem sits below. The background is plain white.

What works

  • Clean, bold and easy to read from far away.
  • The white background disappears into the bag, so there’s no square edge.
  • The simplest design here, so it is the safest to press.

Fix before pressing

  • There is a wide gap between the title and the pumpkin. Move the pumpkin up or make it a little bigger.
  • The light lavender letters turn a dusty gray-purple on tan canvas. The dark outline keeps them readable, but a deeper purple fill will look brighter.
  • Optional: add a few orange bats near the pumpkin so the top and bottom feel connected.

Proof 13 of 13 Untitled Design 13.png

Untitled Design 13

BOO! Sampler

Small fixesA few edits in Canva

What’s on it

A white background scattered with Halloween pieces: a black sign with white "Happy Halloween" and sparkles, two cute gray bats, a black ghost, drippy "BOO!" letters, candy corn, wrapped candy, spiders on webs, flying bats and cobwebs in the top corners. Strips of candy and ghost icons run along the top and bottom.

What works

  • Lots of fun, kid-friendly pieces.
  • The black sign keeps the title readable. The white letters will print tan, which still shows clearly on black.

Fix before pressing

  • The pieces are scattered without a clear plan. Group them: title in the middle, BOO! and the ghost on one side, bats on the other.
  • The bottom candy strip has a gap in the middle. Make it one continuous strip like the top.
  • Cut a few of the black bats. There are eight, and they crowd the right side.
  • Rename the file to "Trick or treat Bag 12" so it fits the set (there is no Bag 12 right now).
